raw_response:
I've farmed this land for 40 years and I know Quzhou's soil and climate in my bones. The sandy loam here drains fast, summer gets hot, and without careful irrigation management my cotton suffers. At 65, I'm not changing what works — but I've kept up with variety improvements and I'm not afraid to use them.

This year I'll plant the full 5 mu in cotton, same as always. I'll use a hybrid variety — the newer Ji-mian hybrids give me better boll size and some tolerance against fusarium wilt, which has been a headache on plots nearby. I'll do rotary tillage in late March to break up the compacted layer from last season, then lay my base fertilizer before transplanting seedlings in late April.

Nitrogen is critical for cotton boll development — I'll apply roughly 18 kg per mu across the season, split between base and top-dress applications at squaring and boll-setting stages. I'll put down phosphorus and potassium as base dressing. My well gives me control that rain-dependent farmers don't have — I'll irrigate at planting, flowering, boll-setting, and late boll-opening: four times. I won't over-irrigate; the roots need to work.

Pest management is the hardest part. Bollworm, aphids, red spider mites — they rotate pressure on you all season. I'll scout weekly and spray about six times, targeting the peak pressure windows. I won't spray blindly on a calendar. After 40 years I can tell when thresholds are crossed.

I expect around 320 kg of seed cotton per mu. A good year with proper boll-setting could push 340, but I plan conservatively.
